questions.q: How did rising oxygen levels contribute to multicellular life?
a: Single cells clustered together to escape oxygen
Oxygen directly created the first living cells
It cooled the planet so plants could grow
It removed all competing organisms
questions.why: Lesson 1 says single cells huddled together to escape oxygen and eventually formed the first multicellular life.

questions.q: Why could giant insects and scorpions exist 300 million years ago?
a: Atmospheric oxygen was about 35 percent
Gravity was much weaker at the time
Predators were almost entirely absent
The climate stayed permanently cold
questions.why: Lesson 2 says atmospheric oxygen was about 35 percent 300 million years ago, allowing giant animals.

questions.q: Why can't ancient giant dragonflies fly in today's air?
a: Today's 21 percent oxygen gives too little lift
Their wings were too fragile to survive
Modern predators catch them quickly
Their bodies became too heavy for air
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that giant dragonflies could not generate enough lift in today's 21 percent oxygen.

questions.q: How does breathing relate to aging, per the summary?
a: It produces toxic byproducts that build up over time
It slowly wears out the lungs and nothing else
It has no measurable effect on lifespan
It speeds aging only in high-metabolism animals
questions.why: Lesson 3 says breathing produces toxic byproducts that accumulate and determine how fast we age.

questions.q: What does the horse and squirrel comparison show?
a: Animals can use similar lifetime oxygen at very different rates
Larger animals always live longer than small ones
Metabolic rate does not vary between species
Oxygen intake is fixed for every species
questions.why: Lesson 3 compares a horse and a squirrel that consume similar lifetime oxygen at different rates.
